final_report.summary: This mission delivered two distinct improvements to the Mission Suggestions system. First, a sort direction toggle button (Asc/Desc) was added to the suggestions panel, giving users full bidirectional control over all existing sort fields (Priority Score, Date Created, Health Status). When sorting by Date Created in descending order, the newest mission always appears at the top as requested. Second, the af_engine.py suggestion generator was updated to write a notification entry to the activity log (chat_history.json) every time it auto-generates a suggestion, so users can see in real time when suggestions are being produced. Both features were implemented cleanly without breaking existing functionality, passed adversarial testing with a spec alignment score of 0.95 and an epistemic score of 0.92.
key_achievements: Added a toggleSortDirection() function to modals.js that switches between ascending and descending order across all sort fields
Added currentSortDirection state variable ('asc'/'desc') integrated into applySortToRecommendations() via a direction multiplier
Added the 'Desc / Asc' toggle button (#rec-sort-dir-btn) to the suggestions toolbar in main_bundled.html
Exported toggleSortDirection from main.js so it is callable from the HTML onclick handler
Updated af_engine.py suggestion pipeline to write '[SUGGESTION] Mission suggestion generated: ...' notifications to the activity log (chat_history.json) on every auto-generation
Activity log entries include mission title and source type (mission completion, drift halt, or manual)
challenges_overcome: The existing sort logic hard-coded the sort direction per field, requiring a refactor to extract a direction multiplier applied uniformly across all comparison branches
Wiring the new button into the webpack-bundled module required re-exporting the function through main.js to the global window object
Writing to chat_history.json safely required using the existing atomic_update_json utility with a fallback default
lessons_learned: The modals.js sort pattern is well-established, making it straightforward to extend with a direction multiplier
Activity log entries from system events should use a 'system' provider and a clear prefix (e.g. '[SUGGESTION]') for visual distinction
Wrapping activity log writes in try/except with debug-level logging on failure keeps the critical suggestion pipeline alive
